title: OTPlace-Vias: A Novel Optimal Transport Based Method for High Density Vias Placement in 3D Circuits
problem: Inter-tier vias placement in Monolithic 3D (M3D) integrated circuits presents significant challenges due to high density requirements and computational complexity scaling in 3D IC manufacturing.
motivation: 3D ICs with M3D technology achieve higher integration density but require efficient computational solutions for complex placement problems at scale.
method: The approach frames inter-tier via placement—positioning vertical electrical connections between layers in 3D circuits—as an optimal transport problem. Optimal transport is a mathematical method that finds the most efficient way to move or arrange objects by minimizing total distance or cost. This formulation naturally breaks into thousands of independent calculations, each handling a small part of the problem. By running these calculations simultaneously on GPUs (graphics processors), the method solves high-density via-placement problems much faster than traditional single-processor approaches.
key_novelty: Optimal transport theory enables GPU-parallelizable solutions to inter-tier via placement.
contributions: Novel optimal transport formulation for inter-tier vias placement problem
GPU-parallel algorithm achieving significant speedup versus prior methods
Effective handling of high integration density circuits

metrics.speedup: significant speedup reported versus previous methods

primary_theme: optimal transport for 3D IC vias placement
